analysis.investment_thesis: Inox Green fails catastrophically on both Magic Formula metrics: Earnings Yield of ~0.8% (EBIT ₹52 Cr / EV ₹6,724 Cr) and ROIC of ~2.4% (EBIT ₹52 Cr / Invested Capital ~₹2,195 Cr) — far below my minimum thresholds of 12% and 20% respectively. Compounding the problem, this is a utility/infrastructure company that Greenblatt explicitly excludes from the Magic Formula because capital structure distorts the metrics.
key_strengths: Debt dramatically reduced: Borrowings fell from ₹1,411 Cr (2021) to ₹95 Cr (2025), nearly debt-free
First profitable years in 2024-25 after years of losses — at least EBIT is positive
Captive O&M pipeline tied to Inox Wind's growing installed base provides revenue visibility
key_risks: Earnings Yield of 0.8% is 15x below my minimum threshold — EV/EBITDA of 129x is speculative bubble territory
ROIC of 2.4% and ROE of 1.02% mean the business destroys value relative to cost of capital
Revenue contracted 7Y CAGR of -6.1% and EBITDA is in a contracting trend — not a growth business
red_flags: Utility sector — explicitly excluded from Magic Formula; capital-heavy model structurally depresses ROIC
Net profit just ₹22 Cr on ₹6,549 Cr market cap — P/E of 81.6x on razor-thin, declining earnings
Free cash flow was negative 4 of last 5 years; operating CF only positive 3/5 years
Other Income ₹57 Cr in 2025 exceeds EBIT ₹52 Cr — underlying operating business is barely earning anything
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula cannot meaningfully endorse this stock. Earnings Yield is 0.77% against my minimum threshold of 12% — meaning you are paying 129x EBITDA for a business earning almost nothing. ROIC of ~2.4% is one-tenth my required threshold of 25%+. The company spent years losing money (negative net profit every year from 2018-2023) and has only generated token profits of ₹28 Cr and ₹22 Cr in the last two years, while market cap sits at ₹6,549 Cr. That is pure speculation, not value investing.

What little positive exists — near debt-free balance sheet and captive O&M contracts from the Inox Wind ecosystem — is overwhelmed by the valuation absurdity. The business generates ₹52 Cr in EBIT but the enterprise is priced at ₹6,724 Cr. Revenue has actually shrunk at -6.1% CAGR over 7 years. Other income (₹57 Cr) now exceeds operating income (₹52 Cr), meaning core O&M operations are marginally profitable at best. This is a story stock priced on renewable energy thematic hype, not on earnings power. Greenblatt would not touch this.
